claims.statement: Shared Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Remote Infrastructure, Presentation, and Persistence modules have enforced dependency responsibilities, while TFM and TFI own platform UI, adapters, composition, and lifecycle.

TermindPersistence exclusively owns SwiftData models, historical schemas, migrations, and container construction, and the app composition roots retain one container per process rather than silently replacing a failed persistent store.

Desktop app-wide services are coordinated by AppModel while navigation and workspaces remain WindowModel-owned; mobile scenes own navigation while MobileAppModel owns shared live workspaces and process services.

SSH connection attempts use one-shot wipeable secret ownership, and interaction-forbidden auxiliary connections reject trust, passphrase, user-presence, and keyboard-interactive work rather than retaining interactive secret material.

SFTP transfer runtime is process-local and coordinates bounded fair admission, connection/channel topology, resumable temporary files, conflict policy, direct remote copy, and external-edit version checks without persisting live connection state.
AgentKit remains the host-neutral runtime boundary while Termind registers host-aware tools, persistence, policy, remote interaction, and native presentation around it.

Vault, Settings, and Metrics retain independent category lifecycles and journals; current-engine fetch completion authorizes uploads, generation checks reject retired work, and overlapping explicit operations and automatic callbacks retain recovery state until safe completion.

Mobile workspace restoration persists connection-free descriptors rather than live sessions, reuses one live workspace across scenes, and detaches transports with asynchronous closure on background expiration while retaining foreground resume intent without implicit approval or execution replay.

V31 adds scoped quarantine and recovery models; released V31 stores migrate directly to V34, which replaces Host, connection-history and Identity models, adds device-directory and Workspace-preference models, and backfills history with the stable installation ID and an initial DeviceRecord without changing independently versioned CloudKit envelopes.

Unsupported or unreadable remote records create scoped persistent upload restrictions checked by journals, restored queues, batches and providers; supported reconciliation atomically clears restrictions, while local pending edits survive retry and restart and compatible records continue syncing.

Connection history synchronizes complete saved-host SSH/Telnet/SFTP events with stable source-device ID, start time and optional end time, while a separate reusable synchronized device directory maps installation IDs to mutable display names; stores deterministically retain 250 events and all-device History surfaces present at most 100 events on desktop and 50 on mobile.

Terminal font family, size and follow-theme-size stay device-local; shared binding-driven controls use an 8–36 editing range with a macOS slider and iOS stepper, while app-owned catalogs include families with any loadable monospaced member and sort using the current locale.

Unavailable and wrong-appearance saved theme names remain selectable without appearance-time persistence; both apps use shared filtered and sorted options and display a fallback while rendering applies the appearance default, custom commands, and finally local typography.
Command history retains at most the shared 250 entries per Host.

AssistantExecutionController synchronously captures composed user-turn content, context, model/provider/credential, reasoning/permissions, search, skills/registry and Guardian/preparation configuration before memory or automatic compaction waits; first-send promotion and edit persistence follow capture.

Preparation has a separate identity from streaming: ordinary cancellation invalidates it synchronously and joins tracked history/preparation work before interrupted persistence; savingFailure instead joins its existing terminal save without cancellation or an added interrupted write. Archive/delete await preparation, edits/forks cannot overtake failure persistence, manual compaction refuses preparation, and changing selection alone does not cancel it.

History edits commit before live replacement, truncate at the selected user message in canonical run/message order, preserve the same-run prefix and its owned tool graph with a neutral completed summary, and prune compactions by removed message boundaries while considering compacted display history for live ownership and title retention.

An edited message first owns its same-ID staging run; the first real snapshot atomically reassigns only the staged row and removes staging while preserving provenance and chronology. Repository-instance retired IDs reject late saves/events. Captured configuration failures project and adopt only after save success and an identity check; rejection reports an error and retires preparation without adoption. Queued-runtime cancellation remains live-before-save, and joining a save attempt does not guarantee storage success.
The captured configuration-failure save task strongly retains its controller and conversation until the attempt returns and preparation retires, including after callers release their handles.

Mobile global background begins only on a transition to a nonempty all-background scene set, including after scene removal; each platform lease is identity-scoped, invalid acquisition expires immediately, stale callbacks cannot affect replacements, and valid identifiers are ended exactly once even if expiration reenters acquisition.

Mobile Assistant expiration synchronously requests cancellation of all conversations before asynchronous retained-owner joins and command/connection cleanup; the composer-send guard lasts until cleanup returns, and the platform expiration handler does not wait for or guarantee completion of those drains under iOS suspension.

Desktop termination fences controller-authorized Assistant admissions, synchronously cancels captured preparation and all app-wide stored conversations, and joins preparation/failure-save attempts and retained runtime consumers with MCP/SFTP before closing Agent background commands and then connections; repeated shutdown returns the same task.

The macOS termination reply independently falls back after three seconds and replies once; captured-turn joins do not guarantee save success or remote-command settlement and exclude manual compaction and title generation, while memory suspension now remains an admission fence until resume reloads state and backfills history.

Shared SSH configuration and pooled connection openings register one continuation per waiter; cancelling one waiter leaves shared work alive for the others, and only the last waiter or explicit Host retirement cancels the underlying opening task.

An MCP upload disconnect synchronously cancels the attempt's transfer token and separately records disconnect provenance, so the response maps to cancellation and remains resumable without treating unrelated SFTP failures as HTTP disconnects.
